verification_causes_recorded: the builder's 2719/2719 claim: the installed-surface suites (interview-cutover) build their fixture installs from the COMMITTED HEAD via git archive, and the builder ran PRE-commit — its installed-surface tests exercised the PRE-fix-round bin, so the recorder-verbs wiring defect was invisible to its run. Demonstrated by the post-commit cutover run failing 4/15 at the identical tree the builder had reported green.

the orchestrator's own subsequent 2719/2719 verification: the aggregated suite output prints one summary per xargs chunk and the verification read only the last chunk's summary (tail -3); the 4 cutover failures sat in an earlier chunk. Demonstrated by the per-file run at the same tree.
both mechanisms are recorded as demonstrated; neither is offered as a general explanation for other green results.

coverage_limits_recorded: the exhaustive kill-between-every-write promotion crash matrix remains unperformed (lens 2's honest limit). The named crash classes ARE covered (mid-flight expected-revision abort, the crash-after-event cache-convergence path, the §10.3 fixture rows), but no test kills the process between every consecutive pair of writes across both artifacts + state + the doc + the refs. The live release rehearsal exercises REAL kill points but is a distinct exercise, not this matrix. Retained as an explicit limitation for the gate-of-record reviewer to judge.

attestation_constraint_recorded: no future evidence receipt may carry attested_by:'user' with an invented question and answer: the operator's standing execution authorization is NOT evidence that the user answered a specific approval question. Any evidence requiring a user-attested receipt either quotes the operator's actual words naming that decision or is not created. (The 2026-09-07 ledger-amendment approval draft in /tmp was never applied — the bundle was unarmed, no capture, no identity to amend — and is retained only as a negative example of this constraint.)
discipline: one review round, one fix round per iteration; every fix round disclosed as not re-reviewed at the iteration that spawned it, with the NEXT iteration covering the fix's own seam; historical verdicts are never rewritten as approvals
